title: Filling cells quickly
summary: Copy a cell to the cells below it or beside it, type the same value into several cells at once, and add a new line inside a cell.
intro:
Instead of dragging the fill handle with the mouse, select the range and press one shortcut: Excel copies the first cell into the rest. If that first cell holds a formula, its references adjust on every row.

You will also learn to type the same value into several selected cells at once, and to start a new line inside a single cell.

faq.a: Yes. It copies the formula from the top cell into the selected cells below, and relative references change on each row, just as if you had dragged the fill handle.

faq.q: Why doesn't Enter start a new line inside the cell?
faq.a: Because Enter confirms your entry and moves to the next cell. For a new line inside the cell, press Alt+Enter, or Option+Return on a Mac.

fill-down.prompt: `B2` holds a formula and you have selected `B2:B10`. To copy it into the cells below, press `Ctrl+D` (on Mac: `⌘+D`).

fill-right.prompt: Now you want to copy cell `B2` into the next cells of the same row, `B2:F2`. Press `Ctrl+R` (on Mac: `⌘+R`).
fill-right.hint: R for Right, towards the next columns.

what-fill-down-copies.prompt: You selected `C2:C6`, and `C2` holds the formula `=A2*B2`. What does `C6` hold after `Ctrl+D`?
options: The result of `C2` as a fixed number
what-fill-down-copies.explain: Relative references change with each row, so the formula on row 6 is `=A6*B6`.

fill-the-selection.prompt: Select several cells, type a value, then press `Ctrl+Enter` instead of Enter: the value goes into every selected cell. On Mac, press `Ctrl+Return`. Try it now.

new-line-in-a-cell.prompt: You are typing a two-line heading in one cell. To start the second line without leaving the cell, press `Alt+Enter` (on Mac: `Option+Return`).
new-line-in-a-cell.hint: Alt with Enter; on Mac, Option with Return.

fill-down-again.prompt: Practice: `D2` holds the total formula and you have selected `D2:D30`. Copy it down with a single shortcut.
fill-down-again.hint: The first letter of the word Down.
